MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









Shape Digital Healthcare. Drive Innovation. Improve Lives. 












About the Department of Clinical Informatics 






The Department of Clinical Informatics is where healthcare and technology come together to transform patient care. 






Established in 2025, we bring together clinical, digital and innovation expertise to shape the future of healthcare across Monash Health. Our multidisciplinary team spans Nursing, Medical, Allied Health and Community Informatics, Digital Clinical Learning and Change, Artificial Intelligence, Consumer Informatics, User Experience and Clinical Coding. 






The Department is committed to building a high-performing team and improving patient outcomes through digital innovation, aligned with the Monash Health Strategic Plan and Digital & Data Plan. 






If you're passionate about innovation, collaboration and using technology to make a real difference in healthcare, this newly created full-time, ongoing role offers the chance to help shape the future from the ground up. 












About the Role 






This ground-breaking role is designed to enable our clinical teams to readily and safely transform patient care, using digital technologies. Intersecting with clinical practice, digital health, change management and workplace capability building, this is a rare opportunity to lead the transition of our clinicians, in all professional streams, to embrace the benefits of a digitally thinking workplace. 






Far from a "Business As Usual" role, this opportunity will suit individuals seeking to leverage strategic leadership and advice to engineer a significant change in the way we deliver patient care. Acknowledging the rapid rate of change in the digital space, you are not deterred by uncertainty. If appointed, you will relish the chance to apply your innovative thinking skills to build diverse, agile, high performing teams. 






As a key member of our Clinical Informatics leadership team, your success will be measured across three key result areas: 









Leadership of change of learning functions and practices 












Collaboration with Clinical Informatics and Digital and Information Division 












Stakeholder engagement and relationship development 









You'll appreciate that the collaborative nature of this role will see you working on site at least three days per week, with flexible working arrangements available. With accountability for the function across the whole of organisation, travel across Monash Health will be required. 












About You 






You have a keen understanding of informatics as well as demonstrated knowledge of adult learning principles. Described as visionary, you also have the ability to translate organisational objectives into practical and effective practices that advance care at the operational level. 






You are comfortable working with ambiguity. Your emotional intelligence equips you with the skills and strategies to navigate the challenges of change respectfully, professionally and sensitively, adapting your style to meet the needs of varying audiences. 






Our clinical teams are highly skilled, busy and saturated with information. Your job will be to enhance their Joy in Work through equipping them with a relevant, digitally-enabled approach that will see them continue to deliver consistently high standards of care in the community we serve. 



What you need 






Your ability to engage and influence effectively across a range of professional groups, pivoting seamlessly between clinical, technical and strategic perspectives, will be key to your success. 






To be considered for this role, you'll need to demonstrate: 









Deep clinical systems expertise and success leading enterprise change 












Strategic leadership of integrated change and learning functions to drive enterprise-wid digitatl transformation 












Intimate appreciation of transformation as it relates to building digital capability 












Expertise in adult learning, enabling success driving digital adoption and optimisation 












Awareness of digital architecture and how systems communicate, share, exchange and use data 












Detailed knowledge of clinical safety and risk management 












Data and information fluency 









Current Ahpra registration, a postgraduate qualification in Digital Health, Informatics, Learning-Education, Change Management and-or leadership are required. 












Why join Monash Health? 






This is more than a digital role-it's your chance to transform healthcare at scale. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day 












At Monash Health, you will: 









Lead a state-wide service with real impact 












Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation 












Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders 












Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes 















We offer: 









The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience 












A supportive, collaborative team environment 












Ongoing learning and development opportunities 












The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service













For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Anthony Pham, Deputy Chief Nursing and Midwifery Information Officer on 0435 968 584.

Requisition ID: CAM29775 - Central Coast Local Health District - Emergency Medicine - Senior Resident Medical Officer

Central Coast Emergency Medicine:

Gosford and Wyong Hospitals contain busy mixed Emergency Departments with a wide variety of presentations, providing excellent exposure to trauma, Paediatrics (~25% of presentations), Medicine, and Surgery. Both are well supported by passionate Emergency Physicians and Trainees who are committed to your development and wellbeing.

In conjunction with the University of Newcastle, CCLHD has recently opened the Central Coast Clinical School and Research Institute on the Gosford Hospital campus, providing additional opportunities in training and research.

Emergency Medicine Training: 

Emergency SRMOs have access to a weekly Consultant-led education program which focuses on procedures, hands-on skills, and Simulation. CCLHD holds several formal courses throughout the year, including BEST (Basic Emergency Skills and Techniques), BASIC (Basic Assessment and Support in Intensive Care), MIMMS (Major Incident Medical Management and Support), DAW (Difficult Airway Workshop), and The Chest Tube Workshop. There is support and career opportunities available for those looking to progress into Emergency Medicine training.

Emergency SRMOs are rostered 8 x 10 hour shifts a fortnight with minimal un-rostered overtime, any of which is paid.Roster matching for couples will be considered.Rotations support the prerequisite to join ACEM with 6 months in Gosford Emergency Department and 6 months in Wyong Emergency Department.

The NSW Central Coast is located only 1 hour north of Sydney CBD.Career opportunities are available for JMOs wishing to progress a career in Emergency Medicine or Critical Care Medicine from SRMO to Consultant level. You will enjoy the benefits of a relaxed coastal lifestyle paired with a rewarding career supporting a rapid growing population that is expected to grow to 450,000 before 2030.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     ICU Clinical Nurse - Equipment Portfolio





Job no: 942385

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide Metro Northern

Categories: Nursing-Midwifery




 

Northern Adelaide Local Health Network - Lyell McEwin Hospital - ELIZABETH VALE SA 5112

Salary: $90,913 - $114,917 p.a. - RN2C

Ongoing Full-Time 

About the Role:

Lyell McEwin Hospital's Intensive Care Unit is one of South Australia's busiest northern metropolitan ICUs, delivering high-acuity care to a diverse and growing community. If you combine sharp critical care clinical skills with a genuine interest in equipment governance, procurement, and education, this full-time ongoing role was designed with you in mind.

What You'll Be Doing in the ICU

Act as the primary clinical lead for ICU equipment management - overseeing procurement advice, maintenance coordination, and lifecycle planning across the unit's device portfolio.

Develop and deliver equipment competency education and orientation programmes for ICU nursing staff.

Partner with nursing, medical, and biomedical engineering teams to evaluate new equipment and ensure safe, evidence-based integration into clinical practice.

Provide direct patient care in the ICU on early shifts (8-hour days), maintaining and modelling current critical care nursing standards.

What You'll Bring

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA and demonstrated ICU or critical care experience.

Proven knowledge of ICU equipment - ventilators, infusion systems, monitoring devices - and confidence guiding others in their safe use.

Experience in or appetite for a clinical educator, coordinator, or specialist nursing role.

Strong communication skills and the ability to influence practice across a multidisciplinary team.

Familiarity with SA Health or NALHN equipment governance frameworks, or the capability to quickly work within them.

Ability to work a consistent early shift, 8-hour day roster as part of a full-time ongoing commitment.

 To be eligible for this position, you must be registered or eligible for registration as a Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and who holds, or who is eligible to hold, a current practicing certificate.

About You:

You will be joining a dynamic and expanding Local Health Network that is committed to delivering contemporary, innovative and high-quality health services within modern facilities.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team.

About Adelaide:

About Us:

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management.

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community.

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services:

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services.

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services.

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care.

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings.

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites.

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains.

Benefits of working at NALHN:

From salary packaging to flexible working arrangements, a large range of opportunities for movement and career progression, you'll find there are lots of benefits of working with Northern Adelaide Local Health Network.

Salary packaging is an option for saving money by paying for some of your everyday expenses from your salary before it is taxed.

Relocation assistance may be available for successful applicants from interstate or overseas.

NALHN supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if you have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working including part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check.

Check(s): 

DHS Working With Children Check (WWCC)

National Police Check (National Police Certificate) for vulnerable person-related employment screening - apply to any of the accredited bodies approved to offer a service direct to the public. Accreditation is provided by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission. See our National Police Certificate accredited bodies page for links to lodge screening requests.

Immunisation Risk for this position is - Category A (direct contact with blood or body substances)

Looking for a clean, immaculate workshop environment in the Western Suburbs?  
 
 
  Tired of dirty, greasy labouring roles and ready to learn high-spec assembly work?  
 
 
  Do you take immense pride in your workspace and possess strong attention to detail?  
 
 
  Want a stable, full-time permanent day shift that guarantees a great work-life balance?  
 
 
 If you are a reliable, hands-on Trade Assistant or mechanical labourer who wants to work in a pristine environment with high-end equipment, this is a fantastic opportunity. Our client is a rapidly expanding, premium original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specialising in high-spec industrial fluid systems and custom pump packages for the Australian mining sector. 
 Due to a sustained growth phase across the business, they are expanding their state-of-the-art production facility and require a dedicated Trade Assistant to support their mechanical engineering team. 
  The Opportunity: Clean Working Conditions & True Team Support  
 Forget chaotic construction sites or dirty wrecking yards. This position is based entirely inside a massive, exceptionally neat, tidy, and organised warehouse. Because this equipment is built strictly to high-level mining regulations, cleanliness and order are central to everything they do. 
 You will be working directly alongside qualified Tradespeople, handling the critical foundational tasks that keep the assembly lines moving smoothly. 
  What You Will Do:  
 Operating on a secure, permanent full-time day shift (Monday to Friday), your responsibilities will include: 
 
 
  Fitter Support:  Assist qualified Mechanical Fitters with the assembly, positioning, and mounting of heavy-duty industrial pumps and diesel/electric engine packages. 
 
 
  Component Handling:  Support the preparation and layout of structural skids, specialised pipework networks, hydraulic hoses, and system sensors. 
 
 
  Workshop Logistics:  Manage the flow of tools, parts, and materials to ensure the assembly floor operates at maximum efficiency. 
 
 
  Pristine Housekeeping:  Maintain an exceptionally clean, organised, and safe workshop floor, ensuring all workspace layouts adhere to strict safety standards. 
 
 
  What's In It For You?  
 
 
  Earning Stability:  A secure, full-time permanent base rate of  $30.00-35.00 per hour + Super , providing long-term career stability. 
 
 
  Genuine Work-Life Balance:  Enjoy a highly structured, predictable day-shift routine with zero forced overtime or sudden weekend rosters. 
 
 
  Premium Environment:  Work within a bright, clean, and highly sophisticated manufacturing warehouse alongside a supportive team. 
 
 
  Real Career Longevity:  This business is growing quickly, making it the perfect time to get your foot in the door with an industry leader. 
 
 
  What You Bring:  
 
 
  The Experience:  A proven background working as a Trade Assistant, workshop labourer, or within a mechanical manufacturing/assembly environment. 
 
 
  The Hand Skills:  High competence using a variety of hand tools, power tools, and workshop machinery safely. 
 
 
  The Attitude:  Absolute pride in your work. We need someone who is punctual, reliable, and notices the little things-maintaining a tidy floor and an organised assembly layout. 
 
 
  The Commute:  Reliable transport to get to the Derrimut workshop for a prompt daily start. 
 
 
  Ready to step up into a clean, modern OEM manufacturing facility?  
  APPLY NOW!  
  Want to chat about the specific workspace setup, the company culture, or the shift times? Call Elliott on 0436 470 032 for a completely confidential discussion.   Please  click here  to apply.
